title: Match the mitigation to the failed MoE stage
description: Inject a production symptom, choose a response, and compare its effect on drops, tail latency, load, and availability.

incidents.label: One expert receives most tokens
incidents.detail: A domain shift concentrates router probability on one expert and capacity alarms rise.
signals: Expert assignment histogram and coefficient of variation
Router entropy, logit magnitude, and auxiliary loss

router-regularization.verdict: Correct the routing objective, then retune capacity
router-regularization.detail: Balancing pressure and router-logit stabilization address the skew itself. Revalidate quality because forcing uniform traffic too aggressively can erase useful specialization.

capacity-headroom.detail: Extra capacity absorbs part of the hot load, but the router remains collapsed. Memory and communication grow while the same expert stays a tail-latency bottleneck.

topology-aware-placement.verdict: Placement cannot repair a collapsed router
topology-aware-placement.detail: A shorter network path may reduce dispatch time, but it does not change which expert receives tokens or prevent capacity overflow.

redundant-experts.verdict: Replication helps availability, not routing quality
redundant-experts.detail: A replica can serve hot work, but assignment skew, synchronization cost, and expert-quality drift remain. Fix the router before treating replication as the primary answer.

incidents.label: All-to-all latency dominates
incidents.detail: Expert compute is fast, but cross-host dispatch saturates one fabric link and p99 jumps.
signals: Bytes and queue time by source-destination device pair
Dispatch, expert-compute, and combine latency spans

router-regularization.verdict: Balanced experts can still overload the wrong links
router-regularization.detail: Load balance improves device compute, but a topology-blind assignment can preserve the same oversubscribed network cut.

capacity-headroom.verdict: More expert capacity increases pressure on the blocked path
capacity-headroom.detail: Allowing more assignments per expert does not add link bandwidth. It can increase in-flight buffers and make the tail worse.

topology-aware-placement.verdict: Keep common routes local and spread collective traffic
topology-aware-placement.detail: Topology-aware expert placement and routing reduce the congested cross-host cut. Confirm that locality constraints do not create a new expert imbalance.

redundant-experts.verdict: A replica is useful only when routing uses its locality
redundant-experts.detail: Duplicating weights adds memory but does not reduce communication unless the router or dispatcher deliberately selects the local copy.

incidents.label: A device holding experts fails
incidents.detail: The router still selects unavailable experts, so tokens cannot complete the sparse feed-forward layer.
signals: Expert heartbeat, device health, and assignment failures
Tokens rerouted, retried, or sent through a fallback path
Quality and latency of degraded-mode responses

router-regularization.verdict: A balanced router can still select a dead expert
router-regularization.detail: Regularization shapes traffic during healthy operation. It does not provide another copy of unavailable weights or a tested degraded path.

capacity-headroom.verdict: Unused capacity cannot execute missing weights
capacity-headroom.detail: Healthy experts have spare slots, but the system still needs a compatible reroute, replica, or fallback policy for tokens assigned to the failed device.

topology-aware-placement.verdict: Placement limits blast radius but needs redundancy
topology-aware-placement.detail: Spreading experts across fault domains prevents one host from removing an entire group, yet unique experts on the failed host remain unavailable.

redundant-experts.verdict: Route to a tested replica or bounded fallback
redundant-experts.detail: A version-matched replica in another fault domain preserves the expert path. The rollout must also test rerouting latency, stale replicas, and fallback quality.

mitigations.label: Rebalance and stabilize the router
mitigations.detail: Tune balancing pressure, router z-loss, noise, and admission using measured token slices.

mitigations.label: Increase expert capacity
mitigations.detail: Reserve more slots per expert and accept the extra compute, memory, and communication cost.

mitigations.label: Change placement and locality
mitigations.detail: Place experts across links and fault domains, then route common traffic through local paths.

mitigations.label: Add replicas and a fallback path
mitigations.detail: Keep compatible expert copies in another fault domain and test bounded degraded behavior.
